title: His son's Russian studies and the 1962 Goodman trip
summary: His son, now a Tufts Russian professor, chose his career after traveling with him on Goodman's 1962 Soviet tour.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Your son is a teacher, isn't he?

Yes, he teaches Russian at Tufts University. As a matter of fact, he's more or less the department head. I'm very proud of him, this year he won a large cash prize because he was voted the teacher of the year for Tufts University, both by the faculty and the student body.
Oh, yes. That's beautiful. I read some of these reports and I just wanted you to say it as a matter of record.

You know, it came -- when he graduated high school it was the summer I went to the Soviet Union with Benny Goodman, 1962. And I didn't really want to go and I was putting up all kinds of obstacles, asking a ridiculous price and then I said I wanted to take my wife, and Gertrude said she couldn't go and leave the children. So I said, well, I want to take my son. Benny said, 'Well, I'll give him a job in the band,' which later he didn't but I took him anyhow. Which was difficult, to take a member of the family to the Soviet Union. The state department of the Soviet Union's against it.

So I took him along with me and when he went to college he was going to be a chemist. And he thought about it and decided he wanted to study Russian because he wanted to go in the State Department. And he talked to the people in the Embassy in Moscow and he said, these people are hopeless, you know. They want war with the Soviet Union and everything else. He said, I feel I should do something for the government so I think I'll study Russian and go into the diplomatic service. But later he felt he'd rather be a scholar and he wound up going to the University of Moscow and he got his Doctor's degree and now he teaches at Tufts. So all from the trip with Benny Goodman.
That's beautiful. That's nice to hear.
